page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the c3d server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor using x86_64 architecture with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 32 GB of system memory, providing 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a single local NVMe SSD with a capacity of 402 GB. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% during stress-ng testing, while multi-core performance falls within the middle 50%. Text processing benchmarks also show strong results. However, memory bandwidth presents a notable performance tradeoff. While cached read-only small block memory bandwidth is average, uncached large block read-only bandwidth is weak, and large block write bandwidth is poor, falling into the bottom 10%. LLM inference speeds are average for small models but drop to weak for medium model prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a dedicated 402 GB local NVMe SSD provides high local storage density relative to the 8 vCPU compute allocation, making it a viable option for workloads requiring fast scratch space without the overhead of network-attached storage. The balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average database operation benchmarks suggest a fit for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations that are not heavily constrained by large-block memory write speeds.
